Covering the four main bases: Chiang Khan, Phu Ruea, Dan Sai, and Loei city. Starting from around ฿300–1,750/night.

introH2: 🏙️ Why does choosing the right base in Loei matter?
introHtml: Loei is a mountain province where the sights are spread far apart. Chiang Khan sits on the Mekong, about 50 km from Loei city — old-wood walking street, sticky-rice alms at dawn, and the Kaeng Khut Khu rapids. Phu Ruea lies the other way, about 50 km out, a cool-climate zone of mountain views, vineyards and Phu Ruea National Park. And Dan Sai is further still, the home of Phra That Si Song Rak and the Phi Ta Khon festival. Meanwhile Loei city is the central base, close to the airport and shops. Many people book without thinking about which zone they'll explore, then end up driving hours back and forth each day. This guide rounds up 10 Loei hotels we've picked across every tier — from Mekong-side boutiques to mountain resorts, down to value guesthouses — each with an honest take from real reviews, prices compared on 3 sites, and direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Loei has no metro and little public transport — renting a car or motorbike is by far the most practical option, especially as Chiang Khan, Phu Ruea and Dan Sai all lie in different directions. Within Loei city you'll find a few songthaews and motorbike taxis. Loei Airport (LOE) is about 10 minutes from the city and around an hour from Chiang Khan. The main bases in this guide: Chiang Khan — the Mekong, the walking street, Kaeng Khut Khu, sticky-rice alms · Phu Ruea — cool air, mountain views, vineyards, Phu Ruea National Park · Dan Sai — Phra That Si Song Rak, the Phi Ta Khon festival · Loei city — the central base, near the airport and shops.

entries.name: Chiangkhan River Mountain Resort
entries.revCount: 156 reviews · highest score in this list
entries.storyHtml: The highest score in this list at 9.1 across 156 reviews — Chiangkhan River Mountain is a riverside boutique resort on the Mekong in Chiang Khan, with both river-view rooms and a pool, which is rare in the old-wood quarter. The Deluxe and Suite rooms on the river side open out to the Mekong and the Lao bank, ideal for sunrise and morning mist. Real reviews praise the riverfront views, the cleanliness and a location an easy drive from the walking street — a stay that stands out for its views and comfort in Chiang Khan.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Pick a River View room if your budget stretches — the Mekong at sunrise is the highlight — and pack a warm layer, as the riverside gets cold in the cool season.
pros: Riverfront on the Mekong, lovely views of the river and Lao bank
Has a pool — rare in Chiang Khan's old-wood quarter
River View rooms open to the water, good for sunrise
Reviews praise the cleanliness and proximity to the walking street
cons: River-view rooms fill up fast in the cool season and on holidays — book ahead
On the riverfront, so it's easier to drive than walk to the walking street

entries.name: Baan Suan La Moon
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Near the walking street · Chiang Khan
entries.addr: 91/11 Moo 1, Soi 5 Bon, Chiang Khan, Chiang Khan district
entries.storyHtml: Baan Suan La Moon is a house-in-a-garden stay near the Chiang Khan walking street, heavily reviewed with 344 reviews and a 9.1 score — matching the list's number one. The draw is the quiet garden setting, where every room looks out onto greenery, run personally by an owner who's warm and hands-on. It's a walk to the walking street and the riverfront, starting at just ฿750. Real reviews praise the cleanliness, the quiet and the owner's care — a fit for those who want a garden-house feel near the old town on a budget.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: It's a small property and fills up on walking-street nights, so book ahead for Friday–Saturday; if there are four of you, the Quadruple room beats booking two rooms.
pros: Heavily reviewed (344) with a high 9.1 score — lots of real data
Quiet garden setting, every room with a garden view
Owner-run and warm — reviews praise the welcome
Walk to the Chiang Khan walking street, great starting price
cons: It's a garden guesthouse — no pool or big-hotel services
Limited rooms, fills up fast on holidays

entries.name: Loei Palace Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Central Loei city · Charoen Rat Rd
entries.addr: 167/4 Charoen Rat Rd, Kut Pong, Mueang Loei
entries.storyHtml: Loei Palace is a 4-star city hotel in central Loei, the highest-scoring of the in-town hotels, with a 9.0 across 106 reviews. It's a larger hotel with spacious rooms, a pool and parking, set in the heart of Loei city near the shops and government offices — easy to get around. It works well as a central base from which to drive out to Chiang Khan, Phu Ruea or Dan Sai on day trips. Real reviews praise the room size, the cleanliness and the central, convenient location.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Step up to a Grand Deluxe, which is roomier and newer than the standard Deluxe, and consider this place if you're using Loei city as a base to drive around the province.
pros: 4-star city hotel, high 9.0 score across 106 reviews
Has a pool and parking, spacious rooms
Central Loei city location near shops, easy to get around
Good base for driving out to Chiang Khan·Phu Ruea·Dan Sai
cons: An in-town hotel — no resort-style nature views
Some fittings are older-style hotel, function over design

entries.name: Loei Village Hotel
entries.addr: 17/62 Noen Kaew Rd, Kut Pong, Mueang Loei
entries.storyHtml: Loei Village is a city boutique hotel in Loei with a local style, scoring 9.0 across 80 reviews. What reviews single out is the daily-changing breakfast buffet; it sits on a quiet lane so you sleep well, yet it's still in town and easy for finding food. It's a compact boutique decorated more warmly than the average in-town hotel, with parking. Real reviews praise the cleanliness, the breakfast and the quiet of the location — a fit for those who want an in-town boutique at an accessible price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Don't miss the daily-changing breakfast, and the Deluxe City View is noticeably larger than the Superior if you want a bit more space.
pros: In-town boutique, warmly decorated, 9.0 score
Daily-changing breakfast buffet that reviews love
Set on a quiet lane — restful but still in town
Has parking, accessible starting price
cons: A small boutique — fewer facilities than a big hotel
No pool — an in-town base built for convenience

entries.name: Riverside Chiangkhan Resort
entries.revCount: 379 reviews · the most-reviewed in this list
entries.mrtTag: 📍 On the Mekong · Kaeng Khut Khu, Chiang Khan
entries.addr: 40/11 Ruamjainaruemit Rd, Kaeng Khut Khu, Chiang Khan
entries.storyHtml: Riverside Chiangkhan is a Mekong-side resort at Kaeng Khut Khu, and the most-reviewed in this list with 379 reviews, scoring 8.5. The draw is the riverside wooden chalets that open onto the Mekong and the Kaeng Khut Khu rapids — one of Chiang Khan's favourite viewpoints. It's a little away from the walking street, but you get the full riverside atmosphere and more quiet. Real reviews praise the morning river views and the riverfront setting, though some note the rooms are simple in the riverside-resort style.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Pick a River View room that opens straight onto the water, and waking up to the mist over the Mekong and Kaeng Khut Khu is the highlight here.
pros: Most-reviewed in the list, 379 reviews — lots of real data
On the Mekong at Kaeng Khut Khu, a favourite Chiang Khan viewpoint
Riverside wooden chalets, lovely river views and morning mist
Quieter riverfront atmosphere than the walking-street zone
cons: Rooms are simple in the riverside-resort style, not design-led
A fair way from the Chiang Khan walking street — you'll drive into town

entries.name: With A View Hotel @ Chiangkhan
entries.revCount: 120 reviews · wooden house on the walking street
entries.mrtTag: 📍 On the Mekong · Chiang Khan walking street
tags: 🏚️ Old wooden house on the Mekong
entries.addr: 185 Moo 2, Chai Khong Rd, Chiang Khan
entries.storyHtml: With A View is a wooden riverside boutique right on the Chiang Khan walking street, scoring 8.7 across 120 reviews. The selling point is the location — step out the door and you're on the walking street, in an old wooden house with genuine Chiang Khan character, plus River View rooms that open onto the Mekong. It's a fit for those who want to soak up Chiang Khan's old town on foot and join the dawn sticky-rice alms easily. Real reviews praise the location and atmosphere, even if rooms are compact in the old-wood style.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Choose a River View room if you want the Mekong, and be aware old wooden houses carry sound — the walking street buzzes late on weekends, so pick an inner room if you prefer quiet.
pros: On the Chiang Khan walking street — the most walkable base
Old wooden house on the Mekong, genuine Chiang Khan feel
Has River View rooms that open onto the river
Easy for dawn sticky-rice alms and morning strolls
cons: Compact rooms in the old-wood style, some without a window
On the walking street, which buzzes late on weekends — not always quiet

entries.name: King Hotel Loei
entries.revCount: 44 reviews · budget base in central Loei
entries.addr: 11/8-12 Chum Sai Rd, Kut Pong, Mueang Loei
entries.storyHtml: King Hotel is a budget hotel in central Loei that scores a strong 8.9, starting at just ฿550. What's surprising at this price: rooms are fairly roomy, some with a balcony, plus a Thai-Japanese garden and parking. It sits central on Chum Sai Road, easy for finding food and driving out around the province. Real reviews praise the value, the cleanliness and the room size — a fit for budget travellers who want a roomy central base without big-hotel services.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The Deluxe with a window feels brighter than the Standard, and for a group the ฿1,000 Family room is great value for somewhere this central.
pros: Cheap from ฿550 yet a high 8.9 score
Fairly roomy rooms, some with a balcony
Has a Thai-Japanese garden and parking
Central Loei city location, easy to get around
cons: A budget hotel — no pool or big-hotel services
Some Standard rooms have no window — choose a Deluxe

entries.name: Phurua Sanctuary Resort and Spa
entries.revCount: 11 reviews · mountain resort in Phu Ruea
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Phu Ruea foothills · near Phu Ruea National Park
entries.storyHtml: Phurua Sanctuary is a 4-star resort on roughly 40 rai of hillside grounds in Phu Ruea, scoring 8.6. The draw is space and mountain views — gardens to wander, plus a pool, spa and yoga room — a fit for those who come to Phu Ruea for cool air and want to spend the whole day on the grounds. The open-air Phu Luang restaurant under the macadamia trees is a corner many guests love. Real reviews praise the grounds and atmosphere, but agree the beds are on the firm side and some service details aren't yet polished; with few reviews so far, it lands here.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you like a soft bed, request an extra topper in advance, and pack a warm layer — Phu Ruea nights get cold, especially late in the year.
pros: Spacious hillside grounds with mountain views and gardens to wander
Has a pool, spa, sauna and yoga room
Open-air restaurant under the macadamia trees, lovely setting
Starts in the low thousands for a 4-star mountain-view resort
cons: Beds are on the firm side; the shower hot water is hard to control
Few reviews so far, and some service details aren't yet polished

entries.name: Phu Pha Nam Resort
entries.revCount: 741 reviews · the most-reviewed overall · Dan Sai
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Dan Sai · near Phra That Si Song Rak
tags: 🛕 Near Phra That Si Song Rak
entries.storyHtml: Phu Pha Nam is a 4-star teak resort in the Dan Sai valley, and the most-reviewed in this whole list with 741 reviews, scoring 8.3. The draw is the valley setting on broad grounds ringed by mountains — one of the few resorts of this level in Dan Sai. It works well as a base for visiting Phra That Si Song Rak, touring Phu Ruea, or coming for the Phi Ta Khon festival. The riverside restaurant and breakfast draw praise. Real reviews like the atmosphere and the woodwork, but agree the rooms are aging and the pool/spa sometimes close in low season, which is why it sits here.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a room on the mountain side, away from the road, for the quietest stay and best views — and if you mean to use the pool or spa, call the resort first to check it's open during your dates.
pros: Most-reviewed in the list, 741 reviews — lots of real data
A 4-star valley resort, a rare option in Dan Sai
Near Phra That Si Song Rak and Phi Ta Khon town — a good base
The riverside restaurant and breakfast draw praise
cons: Rooms are aging and rustic in style (opened 2010)
Pool and spa sometimes close for maintenance in low season

entries.name: Sugar Guesthouse
entries.addr: 4/1 Soi 4, Wisutthithep Rd, Kut Pong, Mueang Loei
entries.storyHtml: Sugar Guesthouse is a budget guesthouse in Loei city, starting at just ฿300, scoring 8.8 across 17 reviews. What backpackers love: the owner is warm and speaks fluent English, happy to suggest where to go around Loei, with a relaxed garden and sala to lounge in. There are both cheap fan rooms with a shared bathroom and air-con rooms with a private bathroom. Real reviews praise the owner's friendliness and the budget price — a fit for solo travellers or backpackers using Loei city as a base to head out.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For air-con and a private bathroom, pick the ฿600 air-con room over the fan room, and ask the owner about routes to Chiang Khan/Phu Ruea — the advice is good.
pros: Lowest starting price in the list, from ฿300
Warm, fluent-English owner who suggests where to go
Garden and sala to lounge in, relaxed vibe
Both fan and air-con rooms to suit the budget
cons: A guesthouse — the cheapest rooms are fan with a shared bathroom
Basic facilities, no hotel-style services

advice.bodyHtml: → Sugar Guesthouse ฿300, an in-town guesthouse with a fluent-English owner · or King Hotel Loei ฿550, a roomy budget hotel scoring 8.9

advice.head: Want to sleep riverside, explore Chiang Khan
advice.bodyHtml: → Chiangkhan River Mountain Resort ฿1,400 on the Mekong with a pool, 9.1 score · or With A View @ Chiangkhan ฿1,200, a wooden house on the walking street

advice.head: Want a garden house near the old town, great value

faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about Loei hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which area should I stay in Loei?
faq.a: It depends on which zone you'll explore · Chiang Khan suits the Mekong, the walking street, sticky-rice alms and Kaeng Khut Khu (Chiangkhan River Mountain, Riverside Chiangkhan, With A View, Baan Suan La Moon) · Phu Ruea suits cool air and mountain views (Phurua Sanctuary) · Dan Sai suits Phra That Si Song Rak and the Phi Ta Khon festival (Phu Pha Nam) · Loei city works as a central base near the airport (Loei Palace, Loei Village, King Hotel, Sugar) · Each zone lies in a different direction, so you'll need a vehicle.

faq.q: ❓ How much do Loei hotels cost?
faq.a: Prices vary widely: guesthouses and budget hotels from about ฿300–750 a night · in-town hotels and boutiques around ฿900–1,400 · Mekong-side resorts in Chiang Khan around ฿1,200–1,800 · mountain resorts in Phu Ruea and Dan Sai from about ฿1,500–1,750 · During the cool season and the Phi Ta Khon festival prices rise and rooms fill fast.

faq.q: ❓ Do I need a vehicle in Loei, and how essential is it?
faq.a: Fairly essential, since Loei's main sights lie in different directions — Chiang Khan is about 50 km from the city, Phu Ruea another ~50 km, and Dan Sai further still · Public transport within the province is limited, so renting a car or motorbike is the most practical and flexible option · If you stay on the Chiang Khan walking street you can walk around that quarter, but to reach the other zones you'll need a vehicle.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a Loei hotel?
faq.a: For ordinary weekdays, booking 2–3 weeks ahead is fine · But during the cool season (November–January), Chiang Khan and Phu Ruea stays fill up fast, and during the Phi Ta Khon festival in Dan Sai (around Jun–Jul), rooms sell out months ahead — book 1–2 months in advance or more.

faq.q: ❓ Should I stay in Chiang Khan or Loei city?
faq.a: Staying in Chiang Khan suits a trip focused on the Mekong, the walking street, dawn sticky-rice alms and old-town atmosphere — walkable within the quarter · Staying in Loei city suits using a central base to drive out to several zones (Chiang Khan, Phu Ruea, Dan Sai), near the airport and shops · On a multi-day trip, many people sleep 1–2 nights in Chiang Khan, then move to another zone.

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest for booking Loei hotels?
faq.a: Prices on each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) differ by promotion and period, so we recommend opening all 3 to compare before every booking — each review page in this article gives you the price-comparison links, which can save several hundred baht a night.
